headline: Zoom vulnerability exploited with AI prompts, researchers say
summary: A critical Zoom flaw allowed hackers to hijack devices during meetings, discovered using AI tools with fewer than 20 prompts.
details: Zoom has patched a significant security vulnerability that could have allowed attackers to take over any device participating in a meeting. Researchers at A Security discovered the flaw, which they dubbed 'Zoomsday,' by using publicly available AI models.

The exploit leveraged Zoom's annotation feature, enabling attackers to run malicious code on victims' devices. This could lead to data theft, activation of cameras or microphones, or installation of malware, all without any visible indication to the user.

What's alarming is the ease with which the exploit was developed. Researchers stated that creating a working exploit for such vulnerabilities typically requires extensive effort from elite teams, but they achieved it in a single day using AI agents.

The vulnerability affected Zoom applications across Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, and iOS. Zoom has since released a fix, urging all users to update their software immediately to protect themselves from potential exploitation.

headline_marked: Anthropic [[watermarks AI text]] to comply with EU AI Act
headline: Anthropic watermarks AI text to comply with EU AI Act
summary: The AI maker will embed invisible watermarks in content generated by its models, including Claude, to meet new European regulations.
details: Anthropic has announced that all models released after August 2 will automatically watermark computer-generated text and files. This move is in direct response to the EU AI Act’s Transparency Code, which mandates that AI-generated or edited content be identifiable by other systems.

The watermarks will be embedded directly into the text and are designed to persist through copying, pasting, and some editing. This means the watermark will be present regardless of which Claude product or interface the text originates from, ensuring consistent identification.

For file content, Anthropic is adopting the C2PA open standard for watermarking. The company has stated it will also extend support for older models to include this watermarking feature, aiming for broad compliance across its AI offerings.

While Anthropic has confirmed the watermarking, it remains unclear how much editing a user would need to perform to remove the watermark. The company has been asked for clarification on this aspect of the implementation.

This initiative follows a broader trend in the AI industry to address concerns about AI-generated content and comply with emerging regulations. Platforms like Suno and Substack have also recently implemented measures to flag or watermark AI-created content.
